title: Exact random-order ratio of Best Fit bin packing
formal: Determine the asymptotic random-order ratio \[R_{\mathrm{BF}}=\lim_{M\to\infty}\sup_{I:\operatorname{OPT}(I)\ge M}\frac{\mathbb E_{\pi}[\mathrm{BF}(I^\pi)]}{\operatorname{OPT}(I)}\] of the Best Fit bin-packing algorithm. Benchmark acceptance requires absolute error at most \(1/100\) in this dimensionless constant; exact determination also qualifies.
definitions:
An instance \(I=(s_1,\ldots,s_N)\) is any finite nonempty labelled list of real item sizes in \((0,1]\). A bin has capacity one. A packing assigns every item to a bin with total assigned size at most one, and \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) is the minimum number of nonempty bins over all packings. There is no bound on the number of distinct sizes or a positive lower bound on the smallest size.

Best Fit starts with no bins. For an arriving item of size \(s\), among all existing bins of load at most \(1-s\), it selects one of maximum load and puts the item there. It opens a new bin only if none can accommodate the item. Equal-load ties are broken by the bin's creation order, earliest first. Items are never moved afterward. \(\mathrm{BF}(I^\pi)\) is the final bin count when labels arrive in the order specified by \(\pi\), uniformly distributed over all \(N!\) permutations. Repeated sizes still have distinct labels. The only randomness is this permutation; the adversary fixes the entire list before it is sampled.

For every positive integer \(M\), the supremum ranges over lists of arbitrary length whose optimal bin count is at least \(M\). These tail suprema are nonincreasing and bounded, so the displayed limit is well defined. Equivalently it is the limsup, as \(m\to\infty\), of the largest expected ratio among instances with optimum exactly \(m\). It is not the supremum over all finite optimum sizes: that latter absolute random-order ratio can differ. Nor is it the ratio of two expectations over independently sampled item sizes. Expectations here condition on a fixed adversarial multiset, whose optimum is deterministic.

The scientific target is the asymptotic constant, with vanishing additive effects measured relative to the optimal bin count. The numerical benchmark tolerance is an acceptance rule for that constant, not a multiplicative relaxation of the packing algorithm or a proof of an exact conjectured value.
answer_criterion: Supply a mathematically specified real number \(a\) and a complete Lean-checked proof that \(|a-R_{\mathrm{BF}}|\le1/100\). A proved interval of width at most \(1/50\) qualifies by its midpoint, and an exact value qualifies. Bounds must cover every admissible item list in the limiting worst case. Experiments, a distribution-specific ratio, an absolute-ratio example with bounded optimum, or a certified interval wider than the stated tolerance are insufficient.
context:
Kenyon introduced random-order analysis of Best Fit. The later Albers–Khan–Ladewig paper carefully separates the asymptotic and absolute ratios and raises the general asymptotic lower bound to 1.10. Special restrictions on item sizes are different problems.

Hebbar, Khan and Sreenivas improve the general asymptotic lower bound to 1.144 and the upper bound to strictly below 1.5. Their discussion associates the longstanding conjecture with a value near 1.15, not a proved exact equality to the decimal 1.15. The checked bounds do not yet determine the constant to the benchmark tolerance.
why: The target measures how much a random arrival order improves a classical greedy packing rule.

import_provenance.original_title: The exact random-order ratio of Best Fit bin packing
import_provenance.original_statement: An adversary chooses the item multiset, then its order is uniformly randomly permuted before Best Fit packs it. Determine the asymptotic worst-case expected ratio to OPT; the conjectured value near 1.15 is still separated substantially from the upper bound.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Beating 3/2 is already resolved: the 2024 result gives 1.5−ε for a fixed ε>0 and a lower bound of 1.144. The open problem here is the true ratio.

sentences: An adversary fixes item sizes and a uniformly random permutation determines their arrival.
Best Fit places each item into the fullest bin that can hold it.
The target is its worst expected ratio in the limit of large optimal bin count.
The checked 2024 bounds leave a substantial gap between 1.144 and a value just below 1.5.
Determining the ratio measures how much random arrival order improves this widely used heuristic.
